ⓐis sustained by the flow of the White Nile from
Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there ⓑare
many endangered mammal species, including African
elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million
people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily
through cattle herding. For example, during the dry
season, nomadic people move deeper into the
wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally
occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep,
cows, and goats and ⓒcatching the abundant fish.
The name “Sudd” comes from an Arabic word for
“barriers,” and the wetland historically protected the
people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and
Romans spent centuries ⓓsearching for the starting
point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the
Roman empire, ⓔsent the military to explore the
White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable

The Everglades is a wetland that ⓐstretches from
Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. (A)It functions as a
“biological supermarket.” Many birds and mammal
species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and
shelter, particularly ⓑduring the migration and
breeding seasons. (B)_________________, the Florida
panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was
nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults
ⓒestimating in the wild. But the whole population
in the Everglades National Park ⓓhad recovered to
about 230 by 2017.
(C)_________________, the Everglades is the only place
ⓔwhich American crocodiles and American alligators
coexist. These animals typically inhabit different
ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas
alligators live in fresh water. However, they are
found ⓕliving together where fresh water from
Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida
Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water
to people in Florida, with one out of every three
people relying on the Everglades for drinking water.
ⓖUnless the Everglades is preserved, millions of
people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

(B) • is의 보어 자리에 제시어를 활용해 명사구 Korea’s largest untouched wetland를 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 부연 설명의 분사구문을 콤마(,) 뒤에 연결한다. 분사구문의 의 미상 주어인 Korea’s largest untouched wetland가 ‘(면적 을) 차지하는’ 주체이므로, cover를 능동을 나타내는 현재 분사 covering으로 변형해 쓴다. • covering의 목적어 자리에 명사구 an area를 쓰고, ‘~만 큼 …한’이라는 뜻의 동등 비교 구문(as+원급+as)을 활용 하여 as big as 210 soccer fields를 연결해 완성한다. 17) ④: ⓓ spoiling(망치는) → creating(만드는) 18) (1) ⓒ → estimated (2) ⓔ → where 또는 in which : ⓒ 전치사 with와 명사구 only a dozen adults에 이어져 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’를 이루는 분사가 와야 하며, 명사구 only a dozen adults가 estimate(추정하다)의 대상이므로 estimating을 수동을 나 타내는 과거분사 estimated로 고친다. ⓔ 주어와 자동사로 이루어진 완전한 절(American crocodiles and American alligators coexist)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내 는 선행사 the only place를 수식하는 관계부사절을 이루 어야 하므로, which를 장소의 관계부사 where로 고치거나 선행사와 어울리는 전치사를 써서 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 in which로 고친다. *원래 지문에는 in which가 쓰였음 오답 ⓓ 주어인 the whole population이 자동사로 쓰인 recover (회복되다)의 주체이며, 부사구 ’by 2017‘이 가리키는 과거 시점((2017년)까지 ’회복된 상태였다‘라는 뜻을 나타내므로 능동태 과거완료(had p.p.)인 had recovered는 적절하다. ⓖ 흐름상 ’만약 ~하지 않는다면‘이라는 뜻으로 완전한 절 (the Everglades is preserved)을 이끌어 조건을 나타내는 부사절을 이루므로, 부사절 접속사 Unless는 적절하다. 19) ④: 많은 새와 포유류 종들이 이주와 번식기에 먹이, 물, 그 리고 피난처를 위해 Everglades에 의존한다고 했으며, 플로리다의 많은 사람들에게는 식수를 제공하는 역할을 한다는 내용으로 볼 때, 생물학적 슈퍼마켓의 기능을 한다는 것은 동물과 인간이 살아가는 데 필요한 삶의 자원을 제공한다는 의미이므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘그것은 ’생 물학적 슈퍼마켓‘의 기능을 한다.’가 의미하는 바로 ④ ‘Everglades는 다양한 종들과 인간 모두에게 필수적인 자원을 제공하는 생태계이다.’가 알맞다. 오답 ① Everglades는 주로 그 자체의 경치의 아름다움으로 가치 있게 여겨지는 자연적인 지역이다. ② Everglades는 주로 독특한 지리적 위치에 의해 형성 된 생태계이다. ③ Everglades는 서로 다른 종들과 인간 사이의 오랜 상호작용에 의해 형성된 지역이다. ⑤ Everglades는 종들과 인간이 이용 가능한 자원을 두 고 오랫동안 경쟁해 온 지역이다. 20) ①: (B) 앞 문장에서는 많은 새와 포유류 종들이 Everglades 에 먹이, 물 그리고 피난처를 위해 의존한다는 일반적 인 사실을 제시하고, 이어지는 문장에서는 플로리다 표 범이라는 구체적인 한 종의 사례를 들어, 이러한 의존 관계가 실제로 어떻게 나타나는지를 설명하고 있으므로 ‘예를 들어’라는 뜻을 가진 For example 또는 For instance가 알맞다. (C) Everglades가 ‘생물학적 슈퍼마켓’으로서 많은 새와 포유류에게 먹이, 물과 피난처를 제공한다는 특징에 이 어, American crocodiles과 American alligators가 공존 하는 유일한 곳이라는 또 다른 특징을 추가 설명하는 흐름이므로 ‘게다가’라는 뜻을 가진 Furthermore 또는 What‘s more가 알맞다. 본문변형 (C)는 원래 지문에서 What is more였음 오답 ② 결과적으로 게다가 ③ 예를 들어 그럼에도 불구하고 ④ 대조적으로 결과적으로 ⑤ 그러므로 마찬가지로

Our speed increased as we approached the finish
line, and my teammates worked hard to support
me. When the finish line came into view, I began
my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our
rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same
victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my

The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on

My name is Bliksem, which means “lightning.” My
parents ⓐnamed me this because they wanted me
to be faster than anyone else. ⓑBorn in the
Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than
people, I ⓒlearned riding a bike almost as soon as
I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair.
When I was eleven, ⓓa junior bicycle race held in
our small town. I ⓔentered the race as the
youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked
around the crowd, and I couldn’t believe my eyes!
My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world
champion, was standing there! I ran over and
asked, “You’re Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have
your autograph?” He smiled and said, “If you win,
you can.” Excited by ⓕthat he said, I pedaled
harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was
waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed
me ⓖhis autograph saying, “You outran the others
by two laps! You’re a real racer, kid!”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓒ learned riding → learned to ride (learn은 목적어로 to부정사를 취하며 뒤에 명사구 a bike가 목 적어로 있고 주어인 I가 자전거를 타는 법을 배우는 주체이므 로, learned 뒤의 동명사 riding을 능동형 to부정사인 to ride로 고친다.) ⓓ a junior bicycle race held → a junior bicycle race was held (앞의 부사절(When ~ eleven)에 콤마(,)로 연결되는 주절의 주 어가 명사구 a junior bicycle race이고, 과거 시점(11살 때)의 일 이므로 과거동사가 이어져야 하며, 주어가 ‘열렸던’ 대상이므로 능동태 과거동사 held를 단수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 단수형 과거 be동사를 써서 과거시제 수동태인 was held로 고친다.) ⓕ that he said → what he said (전치사 by의 목적어 자리이므로 명사구나 명사절을 이루어야 하며, 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 형용사절은 올 수 없으 므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~하는 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what 이 said의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(he said)을 이끌도록 that을 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)

Gabriel’s final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250
km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These
(A)[bumpy / smooth] roads were a true test of
endurance, talent, and mental power for every
cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my
strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky
and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could
not (B)[continue / stop]. Gabriel offered me his bike
without hesitation, saying, “I ⓐremember for you
finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when
I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I’ll catch
up.” The rest of the members urged me on and
ⓑwe continued, pushed ourselves to our limits.
When there were only 10 km left in the race,
Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut
in front of me and said, “Save your energy now for
the final sprint. We’ll help you to the finish line.”
Our speed (C)[decreased / increased] as we
approached the finish line, and my teammates
worked hard to support me. When the finish line
came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush
of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail,
fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the
finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

While it is true that individual skills are the most
important in the world of sports, ____________________
__________________________________________________________
is equally important. In a marathon, a key reason a
front runner can reach the finish line after that long
journey is the presence of a pacemaker. The
pacemaker helps maintain a steady pace for the
front runner, shielding the front runner from the
headwind. Without the pacemaker, the front runner
has to cope with the harsh wind alone and put in
extra effort to maintain the pace. In Formula One,
the world’s largest car race series, each team enters
two cars. Both drivers try their best for victory, but
for the team’s win, one person employs strategies
such as blocking or obstructing other vehicles so
that their teammate can get ahead. In rock
climbing, individual skills are essential, but when a
mistake is made, the person referred to as the
belay partner manages the rope to prevent a fall.
Similarly, in the case of scuba diving, all divers are
paired up with a dive companion called a “buddy.”
The buddies are responsible for each other’s safety.
No matter how exceptional your skills may be, you
cannot do it alone.
choices: possessing a mindset that seeks to win at allcosts
focusing on a routine that builds up physicalstrength and stamina
having a partner who can cooperate with theplayer with those skills
analyzing the performance of a rival who mighthinder the player’s victory
selecting a leader who can manage the team’soverall budget and schedule

doughnut shop owners did to make their shops
safer at night.
G: I wonder what they did. ___________________________
___________________
B: It says that doughnut shops in the past were
one of the few places that were open late.
G: Oh, the owners must have been very concerned
for their safety.
B: You’re right.
G: So, what did they do?
B: They came up with the idea to donate leftover
doughnuts to police officers who were on duty
late at night.
G: Ah, because they got free doughnuts, police
officers visited doughnut shops more frequently,
and the owners became safer from potential
robbers.
B: That’s right. I thought that both of them
benefited each other in a creative way.

Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
ⓐregarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this expert architect was
once troubled when designing an amusement park.
He finished most of the main structures except for
the pathways between the attractions. Gropius wanted
to find the best design for the pathways but could
not come up with anything that satisfied him.
(A) In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The
shapes of the paths were not unified, with
some wide and some narrow, because they
were formed naturally by visitors. The following
year, Gropius used the grass pathways as an
outline ⓑwhich he built permanent pathways,
resulting in the most convenient and efficient
routes. This pathway design was later chosen as
the best road design at the 1971 International
Landscape Architecture Symposium in London.
(B) ⓒAstonished by the elderly couple’s idea of
allowing
customers
to
freely
pick
grapes,
Gropius thought it would be good to extend
this idea to the amusement park design and
allow visitors to create their own paths. Upon
returning to his project, he instructed the
construction team ⓓplant grass in areas where
he wanted to create the pathways. When the
grass
started
to
grow,
he
opened
the
amusement park earlier than planned.
(C) One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to ⓔbeing famous for its vineyards.
Farmers were selling grapes along the road near
each vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his
eye because there was no one selling grapes
but only a box by the side of the road. It
turned out that the elderly couple who owned
the vineyard were in poor health and could not
pick the grapes themselves. Instead, ㉠그들은 사
람들이 그 상자에 5프랑을 넣는 한 그들이 원하는
만큼 많은 포도를 따는 것을 허락했습니다. The
couple not only prevented their grapes from
becoming too ripe by permitting grape picking,
but they also provided an enjoyable experience
for their customers.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people
to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could
damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented
for an architect ⓕto let people do the designing.
Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating
ideal pathways by ㉡__________________________________.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 숙련된 건축가인 Gropius가 처했던 문제점으로, 놀이기구 사이 의 통행로에 맞는 최적의 디자인을 떠올릴 수 없었다는 주어 진 글 다음에, Gropius가 프랑스 여행 중 건강이 좋지 않아 포 도를 직접 딸 수 없었던 포도원 주인인 노부부가 사람들에게 (길가에 있는) 상자에 5프랑을 넣는 한 원하는 만큼 포도를 마 음껏 따가도록 한 사실을 알게 되었다는 (C), 앞서 언급된 포 도를 직접 따게 하는 일을 the elderly couple’s idea로 가리켜, Gropius가 이 발상을 확장하여 놀이공원의 통행로를 방문객들 이 만들게 하겠다는 생각으로 건축 팀에게 길을 내고자 한 곳 에 잔디를 심도록 지시했고, 잔디가 자라기 시작했을 때 놀이 공원을 개장했다는 (B), 그가 사람들이 반복적으로 걸어 다닌 곳의 잔디 위에 생긴 오솔길을 윤곽선으로 사용하여 영구적인 통행로를 만들었다는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

solution: ⓑ should be → should have been (흐름상 ‘더 조심했어야 했다’는 뜻으로, 과거에 하지 않은 일 에 대한 후회나 유감을 나타내야 하므로 ‘~했어야 했다’라는 뜻의 should have p.p.를 써야 한다. 따라서 should be를 should have been으로 고친다.) ⓔ was asked the members if → asked the members if (Gabriel이 ‘질문을 받았던’ 대상이 아니라 ‘질문을 했던’ 주체이 므로 과거시제 수동태(was/were+과거분사)가 아니라 과거시제 능동태를 써야 한다. ask는 ‘ask+간접목적어(~에게)+직접목적 어(…을)’의 4형식 구문에 쓰일 수 있고, if는 ‘~인지’라는 뜻의 명사절 접속사로서 목적어 역할의 명사절을 이끌 수 있으므로, 능동태 과거시제 asked 뒤에 간접목적어인 명사구 the members와 직접목적어절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 if가 이어지 도록 asked the members if로 고친다.) ⓖ make him proudly → make him proud (‘~하기로 굳게 결심하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘be determined+to부정 사’를 쓰므로 to 뒤에 동사원형 make가 쓰여 to부정사를 이룬 것과, make가 5형식 동사로서 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’(~을 …하게(…한 상태로) 만들다)의 5형식 구문을 이룬 것은 알맞으 나, 목적어 him에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리에 부사는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사 proudly를 형용사 proud로 고친다.) 천재(조수경) 4과

body:
While it is true that individual skills are the most
important in the world of sports, having a partner
who can cooperate with the player with those skills
ⓐare equally important. In a marathon, a key
reason a front runner can reach the finish line after
that long journey is the presence of a pacemaker.
The pacemaker helps maintain a steady pace for
the front runner, ⓑshielding the front runner from
the headwind. (A)[With / Without] the pacemaker,
the front runner has to cope with the harsh wind
alone and put in extra effort ⓒto maintain the
pace. In Formula One, the world’s largest car race
series, each team enters two cars. Both drivers try
their best for victory, but for the team’s win, one
person employs strategies such as blocking or
obstructing other vehicles so that their teammate
can (B)[fall behind / get ahead]. In rock climbing,
individual skills are essential, but when a mistake is
made, the person ⓓreferred to as the belay partner
manages the rope to (C)[cause / prevent] a fall.
Similarly, in the case of scuba diving, all divers
ⓔare paired up with a dive companion called a
“buddy.” The buddies are responsible for each
other’s safety. No matter how exceptional your skills
may be, you cannot do it alone.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: Withfall behindprevent
Withoutget aheadcause
Withget aheadprevent
Withoutget aheadprevent
Withfall behindcause
solution: (A) 페이스메이커는 선두 주자가 일정한 속도를 유지하는 것을 돕고 맞바람으로부터 선두 주자를 막아 준다고 했으므로, 페이 스메이커가 없으면 선두 주자는 혼자서 강한 바람에 대처하고 속도를 유지하기 위해 추가적인 노력을 해야 한다는 흐름이 되는 Without(~이 없으면)이 알맞다. (B) 포뮬러 원에서 각 팀은 차 두 대를 출전시키며 둘 다 승리 를 위해 최선을 다하지만, 팀의 승리를 위해 한 사람은 다른 차량을 막거나 방해하는 전략을 사용한다고 했으므로, 이는 팀 동료가 앞서 나갈 수 있게 하려는 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한 다. 따라서 get ahead(앞서 나가다)가 알맞다. (C) 암벽 등반에서 개인의 기량이 필수적이라고 한 뒤에 but (하지만)으로 연결되므로 반대 흐름의 내용이 이어져야 하며, 뒤에서 버디는 서로의 안전을 책임진다고 부연하고 있으므로, 실수가 발생했을 때 빌레이 파트너로 불리는 사람이 추락을 방지하기 위해 로프를 관리한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 prevent(~을 방지하다)가 알맞다.

While it is true that individual skills are the most
important in the world of sports, having a partner
who can cooperate with the player with those skills
is equally important. In a marathon, a key reason a
front runner can reach the finish line after that long
journey is the presence of a pacemaker. The
pacemaker helps maintain a steady pace for the
front runner, shielding the front runner from the
headwind. Without the pacemaker, the front runner
has to cope with the harsh wind alone and put in
extra effort to maintain the pace. In Formula One,
the world’s largest car race series, each team enters
two cars. Both drivers try their best for victory, but
for the team’s win, one person employs strategies
such as blocking or obstructing other vehicles so
that their teammate can get ahead. In rock
climbing, individual skills are essential, but when a
mistake is made, the person referred to as the
belay partner manages the rope to prevent a fall.
Similarly, in the case of scuba diving, all divers are
paired up with a dive companion called a “buddy.”
The buddies are responsible for each other’s safety.
No matter how exceptional your skills may be, you
cannot do it alone.
choices: A pacemaker in a marathon helps the lead runnerkeep a consistent speed by blocking the wind.
In Formula One, one driver may use strategiesto block opponents, allowing their teammate tomove ahead.
In rock climbing, the belay partner is expectedto climb alongside the climber to help themreach the top faster.
Scuba diving buddies share a mutual responsibilityfor ensuring each other‘s safety during a dive.
It is just as important for an athlete to have acooperative partner as it is to possess excellentindividual skills.

Sophia: As you know, people from all over the

city’s historical monuments. So, the city had to

carve their names on locks and attach them to a

longer permitted. Even the existing ones have been
removed since 2012. This law was also introduced
in Venice so that locks could no longer damage the
famous Rialto Bridge.
In addition, people are not allowed to go into the
city’s iconic Trevi Fountain. Although you may be
tempted to dip your toes into the cool fountain
water on a hot summer day, it is illegal to do so.
Sitting on Rome’s famed Spanish Steps has also
been banned since 2019. If you don’t follow this
law, you re made to pay a fine ranging from €250
to €450. All of these laws are committed to
protecting the city’s historical monuments.

All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
ⓐwhat people value.
(A) Cultures with high uncertainty avoidance are
uncomfortable with unexpected or unknown
events. Thus, they tend to have strict standards
and guidelines ⓑto prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures
with low uncertainty avoidance are more open
to the unknown and show more acceptance to
things that are different. This is why these
cultures tend to impose fewer regulations.
(B) Another feature that distinguishes cultures ⓒare
their orientation of temporal horizon, or how they
relate to time. Cultures with short-term orientation
emphasize the present over the future. Since
they are more focused on what is happening now,
they place more stress on having immediate
outcomes. However, cultures with long-term
orientation value the future over the present. In
these
cultures,
people
are
likely
to
delay
short-term results in favor of long-term ⓓones.
(C) A psychologist ⓔwas named Geert Hofstede
became interested in cataloging these invisible
cultural features, and he came up with a
number of categories. According to him, a
cultural difference can be found regarding
uncertainty avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance
refers to how well people of a certain culture
tolerate the unexpected.

itself is quite well-known internationally, I imagine
that ____________________________________________________.
Singapore was a small nation with limited resources
when it gained independence.
The nation’s prime minister at the time came up
with strategies to boost national prosperity, one of
which was to transform the nation into an “oasis”
for tourists in Asia. In order to accomplish this, he
emphasized
cleanliness
and
orderliness,
which

body:
All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
what people value. A psychologist named Geert
Hofstede became interested in cataloging these
invisible cultural features, and he came up with a
number of categories. According to him, a cultural
difference can be found regarding uncertainty
avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers to how well
people of a certain culture tolerate the unexpected.
Cultures
with
high
uncertainty
avoidance
are
uncomfortable with unexpected or unknown events.
Thus, they tend to have strict standards and
guidelines
to
prevent
uncertain
things
from
happening. On the other hand, cultures with low
uncertainty
avoidance
are
more
open to
the
unknown and show more acceptance to things that
are different. This is why these cultures tend to
impose fewer regulations. Another feature that
distinguishes cultures is their orientation of temporal
horizon, or how they relate to time. Cultures with
short-term orientation emphasize the present over
the future. Since they are more focused on what is
happening now, they place more stress on having
immediate
outcomes.
However,
cultures
with
long-term orientation value the future over the
present. In these cultures, people are likely to delay
short-term results in favor of long-term ones.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Uncertaintyavoidanceandtimeorientationmainly explain why cultures develop strict lawsand regulations.
Cultural variation can be explained by individualpsychological preferences rather than sharedcultural values.
Cultural distinctions are determined primarily bywhether societies focus on the present or thefuture.
Differences among cultures are largely the resultof social rules designed to control behavior.
Cultures vary according to hidden factors likeuncertainty avoidance and time orientation.
solution: 문화는 각기 다른 특성을 가지고 있으며 문화적 차이가 나타 나는 원인으로 심리학자 Geert Hofstede가 제시한 두 가지 특 성인 불확실성 회피와 시간적 지평성의 방향성에 관한 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 요지로 ❺ ‘문화는 불확실성 회피와 시간 지향성과 같은 보이지 않는 요인에 따라 달라진다.’가 알맞다.

Upo

The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa,
sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake
Victoria in Uganda.
(A) The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries
searching for the starting point of the Nile
River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire,
sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61
AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed
beyond the Sudd.
(B) For example, during the dry season, nomadic
people move deeper into the wetland and build
seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands
to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats
and catch the abundant fish. The name “Sudd”
comes from an Arabic word for “barriers,” and
the wetland historically protected the people
from invaders.
(C) In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal
species, including African elephants and antelopes.
Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland
for a living, primarily through cattle herding.

The Camargue is a region in southern France
where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean
Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It
functions as a natural ⓐsponge, absorbing and
gradually releasing surface water such as rain,
groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold
water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also
an excellent place to observe more than 400
species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and
lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an
ⓑideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool
off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most
famous species found there. The area is also known
ⓒhistorically for its white horses. The Camargue
horses are a special breed, said to be one of the
world’s oldest, and they have spent thousands of
years living in the unique environment of the
Camargue and ⓓadapted to its salty wetlands. They
have become powerful and strong as a result of
surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick
grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever
seen
a
magnificent
image
of
horses
running
through water, it is very ⓔunlikely that they are
Camargue horses from this area.

to analyze the economic benefits derived fromthe Camargue wetlands
to discuss the migration routes of birds passingthrough the Camargue wetlands

The Everglades is a wetland ⓐthat stretches from
Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a
“biological supermarket.” Many birds and mammal
species ⓑrely on the Everglades for food, water,
and shelter, particularly during the migration and
breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther
has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly
extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated
in the wild. But the whole population in the
Everglades National Park had recovered to about
230 by 2017.
What is more, the Everglades is the only place
ⓒwhere American crocodiles and American alligators
coexist. These animals typically inhabit different
ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas
alligators live in fresh water. However, they are
found living together where fresh water from Lake
Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay.
Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to
people in Florida, ⓓwith one out of every three
people relying on the Everglades for drinking water.
ⓔUnless the Everglades is preserved, millions of
people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
what people value. A psychologist named Geert
Hofstede became interested in cataloging these
ⓐinvisible cultural features, and he came up with a
number of categories. According to him, a cultural
difference can be found regarding uncertainty
avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers to how well
people of a certain culture (A)[tolerate / tolerating]
the unexpected. Cultures with high uncertainty
avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or
unknown events. Thus, they tend to have ⓑstrict
standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures with
low uncertainty avoidance (B)[is / are] more open to
the unknown and show more acceptance to things
that are different. This is why these cultures tend to
impose ⓒmore regulations. Another feature (C)[that
/ what] distinguishes cultures is their orientation of
temporal horizon, or how they relate to time.
Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the
present over the future. Since they are more
focused on what is happening now, they place
more stress on having ⓓimmediate outcomes.
However, cultures with long-term orientation value
the future over the present. In these cultures,
people are ⓔlikely to delay short-term results in
favor of long-term ones.

(C)

All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
what people value. A psychologist named Geert
Hofstede became interested in cataloging these
ⓐinvisible cultural features, and he came up with a
number of categories. According to him, a cultural
difference can be found regarding uncertainty
avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers to how well
people of a certain culture (A)[tolerate / tolerating]
the unexpected. Cultures with high uncertainty
avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or
unknown events. Thus, they tend to have ⓑstrict
standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures with
low uncertainty avoidance (B)[is / are] more open to
the unknown and show more acceptance to things
that are different. This is why these cultures tend to
impose ⓒmore regulations. Another feature (C)[that
/ what] distinguishes cultures is their orientation of
temporal horizon, or how they relate to time.
Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the
present over the future. Since they are more
focused on what is happening now, they place
more stress on having ⓓimmediate outcomes.
However, cultures with long-term orientation value
the future over the present. In these cultures,
people are ⓔlikely to delay short-term results in
favor of long-term ones.

MC: Yes, I remember Singapore as a clean and
pleasant country to visit. Sophia, can you tell us
about an interesting law in Italy?
Sophia: As you know, people from all over the
world visit Rome, the capital of Italy. Unfortunately,
some tourists’ actions caused severe damage to the
city’s historical monuments. So, the city had to
establish a number of laws to protect its numerous
historical sites. One of them was to forbid adding a
lock to any bridge in Rome. You may have heard
that to symbolize their love forever, many couples
carve their names on locks and attach them to a
bridge. However, as the weight of the locks
increases the pressure on bridges, they are no
longer permitted. Even the existing ones have been
removed since 2012. This law was also introduced
in Venice so that locks could no longer damage the
famous Rialto Bridge.
(A)_______________, people are not allowed to go
into the city’s iconic Trevi Fountain. Although you
may be tempted to dip your toes into the cool
fountain water on a hot summer day, it is illegal to
do so. Sitting on Rome’s famed Spanish Steps has
also been banned since 2019. If you don’t follow
this law, you are made to pay a fine ranging from
€250 to €450. All of these laws are committed to
protecting the city’s historical monuments.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

Matilde: Sure. Switzerland is very concerned about
the welfare of not only humans, but also animals.
In fact, it is one of the world’s most animal-friendly
countries, earning the support of many animal
lovers. In 2008, the Swiss government made it a
requirement for social animals that typically live in
groups, like goldfish, rabbits, or guinea pigs, to be
kept in pairs. In other words, it is illegal to own
and raise just one goldfish, one rabbit, or one
guinea pig. This law recognizes that social animals
will experience loneliness if left alone and considers
this to be a case of animal abuse. In my case, I
raised two guinea pigs when I was young. When
one of them died, I had to get another one.
Otherwise, I would have been fined. There are
additional laws in place to guarantee animals’
quality of life. For example, Switzerland is known to
be the only European country requiring all dogs to
be microchipped and registered in the country’s
database. This is to stop the illegal trade of dogs.
As these laws suggest, you can tell how much
Switzerland cares about animal welfare.

문장에 언급된 내용에 상응해 ’그렇지 않았다면‘이라 는 뜻으로 쓰여 ’또 다른 한 마리를 데려오지 않았다면‘이 라는 과거 사실에 반대되는 상황을 가정하고 있으며, 가정 법 과거완료(If+S+과거완료(had+p.p.), 주어+조동사의 과거 형+have+p.p.) 구문에서 If절을 대신하는 것으로 볼 수 있 으므로, ’had+p.p.’를 사용해 ‘If I had not gotten another one’으로 전환해야 한다. 오답 ⓐ to share는 목적(~하기 위해서)을 나타내는 부사적 용 법의 to부정사구이므로 ‘in order+to부정사’로 바꿀 수 있 고, that은 unique laws를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 로서 which로 바꿔 쓸 수 있으므로, ‘in order to share 법들)가 가리키는 껌 금지법, 쓰레기 를 적절하지 않게 버리거나 공공장소에서 침을 뱉는 것 을 금지하는 법들이 시행된다는 흐름이 되는 enforced (시행되는)가 알맞다. suspended 보류되는 본문변형 implemented → enforced 16) ②: (A) 로마와 베니스가 자물쇠를 다리에 다는 것을 금지 한 것에 이어, 도시의 상징적인 Trevi 분수에 들어가는 것이 허용되지 않는다는 또 다른 법의 사례를 추가 제 시하고 있으므로 ‘게다가’의 의미를 가진 Furthermore 또는 In addition이 알맞다. *원래 지문에는 In addition이 쓰였음 (B) Matilde, Chen, 그리고 Sophia가 공유한 법 중 일 부는 처음에 이해하기 어려워 보일 수 있다는 내용 뒤 에 이제 그 법들 뒤에 숨겨진 이야기를 알게 되었으니 그 법들이 왜 시행되었는지 이해할 것이라고 확신한다 는 흐름으로 ‘하지만’의 뜻을 가진 However가 알맞다. 오답 ① 요컨대 즉 ③ 예를 들어 하지만 ④ 예를 들어 게다가 ⑤ 게다가 다시 말해서 17) Considering the large number of tourists, it is understandable why Italy passed these regulations to protect its priceless monuments : • ‘~을 고려하면’이라는 뜻으로 전치사의 역할을 하며 관용적으로 쓰이는 비인칭독립분사구문 ‘Considering ~’ 을 활용하여, 제시어 consider를 Considering으로 변형 하고, 목적어로 명사구 the large number of tourists를 쓴다. • <조건>에 따라 ‘가주어(it)-진주어(의문사절)’ 구문을 사용하여 먼저 가주어 it과 동사 is를 쓰고 보어로 형용 사 understandable을 쓴다. 이어서 진주어 자리에 의문 사 why를 사용해 의문사절을 ‘의문사(구)+평서문’의 간 접의문문 어순으로 쓴다. 이때, 주어 Italy 뒤에 제시어 pass를 시제에 맞게 과거형 passed로 변형해 쓴다. • <조건>에 따라 부사적 용법의 to부정사를 활용하되, ‘보호하기 위해서’라는 의미가 되도록 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법을 활용하여 to protect를 쓰고, 목적어로 명사구 its priceless monuments를 써서 완성한다. 18) historic monuments[sites], adding, sitting 제시문 자국의 역사적인 기념물들[장소들]을 보호하기 위 해, 로마는 다리에 자물쇠를 다는 것, 트레비 분수에 들어 가는 것, 그리고 스페인 계단에 앉는 것을 금지하는 법을 가지고 있다. 19) ⑤: 장기 지향성을 가진 문화권에서는 현재보다 미래를 더 중시하며, 장기적 성과를 지지하여 단기적 결과를 미루 는 경향이 있다고 언급하고 있으므로 ⑤ ‘장기 지향성 을 가진 문화에서, 미래는 현재보다 더 많이 가치 있게 여겨지지만, 실제로는 단기적 결과들이 우선권을 가진 다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① Geert Hofstede는 보이지 않는 문화적 특성을 연구 했고 불확실성 회피에서의 문화적 차이를 확인했다. ② 불확실성 회피는 한 문화의 구성원들이 예견되지 못한 사건들을 다루는 정도를 설명한다. ③ 높은 불확실성 회피 문화에 속한 사람들은 예상치 못한 상황에 의해 불안해하며 엄격한 규칙과 지침을 따르는 경향이 있다. ④ 문화적 차이와 관련된 또 다른 특징은 시간 지향성 으로, 이것은 사람들이 시간을 어떻게 인식하는지를 의 미한다. 20) ②: 스위스는 세계에서 가장 동물 친화적인 나라 중 하나 로, 2008년 금붕어, 토끼, 기니피그와 같이 무리를 지어 사는 사회적 동물을 쌍으로 기르는 것을 의무화하고, 개의 불법 거래를 막기 위해 모든 개에게 마이크로칩 을 삽입하고 국가 데이터베이스에 등록하도록 요구하 는 법 등을 시행하여 동물 복지에 매우 신경을 쓴다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ② ‘동물 복지 를 향상시키기 위해 스위스가 취하는 법적 조치들’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 스위스가 동물 복지와 인간의 복지를 균형 있게 유 지하는 방법 ③ 동물의 불법 거래를 막기 위한 스위스의 다양한 법 적 규제들 ④ 스위스가 법적 체계 안에서 동물 복지에 그토록 강 한 강조점을 두는 이유 ⑤ 높은 동물 복지 기준을 유지하는 데 있어 스위스가 직면하는 수많은 도전들

ⓐwhich the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean
Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It
functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and
gradually releasing surface water such as rain,
groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold
water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also
an excellent place to observe more than 400
species of birds. Due to the fact ⓑthat wetlands
and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is
an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool
off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most

known
historically
for
its
white
horses.
The
Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be

of the Camargue and ⓓadapted to its salty
wetlands. They have become powerful and strong
as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where

The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from
Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It ⓐfunctions as a
“biological supermarket.” Many birds and mammal
species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and
shelter,
particularly
during
the
migration
and
breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther
has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly
extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated
in the wild. But the whole population in the
Everglades National Park had ⓑdeclined to about
230 by 2017.
What is more, the Everglades is the only place
where American crocodiles and American alligators
ⓒcoexist. These animals typically inhabit different
ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas
alligators live in fresh water. However, they are
found living together where fresh water from Lake
Okeechobee ⓓmeets the salt water of Florida Bay.
Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to
people in Florida, with one out of every three
people relying on the Everglades for drinking water.
Unless the Everglades is ⓔpreserved, millions of
people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

thegeographicalfeaturesandhistoricalsignificance of the Everglades wetland

the ecological value of the Everglades as ahabitat for many creatures
the seasonal migration and breeding patterns ofEverglades wildlife

The Everglades is a wetland that (A)[stretches / is
stretched] from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It
functions as a “biological supermarket.” Many birds
and mammal species rely on the Everglades for
food, water, and shelter, particularly during the
migration and breeding seasons. For example, the
Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It
was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults
estimated in the wild. But the whole population in
the Everglades National Park had recovered to
about 230 by 2017.
What is more, the Everglades is the only place
(B)[where / what] American crocodiles and American
alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit
different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water,
whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they
are found living together where fresh water from
Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida
Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water
to people in Florida, with one out of every three
people (C)[rely / relying] on the Everglades for
drinking water. ⓐEverglades가 보존되지 않으면, 수백
만 명의 사람들이 식수 부족으로 고통 받을 것입니다.

(B) 주어와 자동사(coexist)로 이루어진 완전한 절(American crocodiles and American alligators coexist)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내는 명사구 the only place를 수식하는 관계부사절을 이 루어야 하므로 장소의 관계부사 where가 적절하다. (C) 전치사 with와 명사구 one out of every three people에 이어져 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+목적어+분사(구)(~가 …한 채로)’ 구문을 이루어야 하므로, 자동사 rely의 현재분사 relying 이 적절하다.

body:
One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye
because there was no one ⓐselling grapes but only
a box by the side of the road. It turned out that
the elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
themselves. Instead, they let people pick as ⓑmany
grapes as they wanted as long as they put five
francs in the box. The couple not only prevented
their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting
grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable
experience for their customers.
Astonished by the elderly couple’s idea of allowing
customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought
ⓒthat would be good to extend this idea to the
amusement park design and allow visitors to create
their own paths. Upon returning to his project, he
instructed the construction team to plant grass in
areas where he wanted to create the pathways.
When the grass started to grow, he opened the
amusement park earlier than planned.
In places ⓓwhere people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some wide and
some narrow, because they were formed naturally
by visitors. The following year, Gropius used the
grass pathways as an outline on which he built
permanent
pathways,
resulting
in
the
most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
ⓔlater chose as the best road design at the 1971
International Landscape Architecture Symposium in
London.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people
to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could
damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented
for an architect to let people do the designing.
Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating
ideal pathways by thinking outside the box.

Why Farmers Should Supervise Their CustomersCarefully
The Traditional Grape-selling Practice of FrenchVineyards
An Elderly Couple’s Ingenious Solution to HarvestingGrapes
Gropius’s Memorable Experience of Picking Grapesin a French Vineyard

One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye
because there was no one selling grapes but only a
box by the side of the road. It turned out that the
elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
themselves. Instead, they let people pick as many
grapes as they wanted as long as they put five
francs in the box. The couple not only prevented
their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting
grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable
experience for their customers.
Astonished by the elderly couple’s idea of allowing
customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it
would be good to extend this idea to the
amusement park design and allow visitors to create
their own paths. Upon returning to his project, he
instructed the construction team to plant grass in
areas where he wanted to create the pathways.
When the grass started to grow, he opened the
amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some wide and
some narrow, because they were formed naturally
by visitors. The following year, Gropius used the
grass pathways as an outline on which he built
permanent
pathways,
resulting
in
the
most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
was later chosen as the best road design at the
1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium
in London.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people
to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could
damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented
for an architect to let people do the designing.
Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into _____________
__________________________ by thinking outside the box.
choices: obeying traditional architectural rules
developing optimal paths for visitors
improving vineyard management strategies
avoiding public involvement in design decisions
maintaining fixed pathways throughout the park

Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this expert architect was
once troubled when (A)designing an amusement
park. He finished most of the main structures
except for the pathways between the ⓐattractions.
Gropius wanted to find the best design for the
pathways but could not come up with anything that
satisfied him.
One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, (B)one far ahead caught his eye
because there was no one selling grapes but only a
box by the side of the road. It turned out that the
elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
(C)themselves. Instead, they let people ⓑpick as
(D)more grapes as they wanted as long as they put
five francs in the box. The couple not only
prevented their grapes from becoming too ripe by
permitting grape picking, but they also provided an
enjoyable experience for their customers.
Astonished by the elderly couple’s idea of allowing
customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it
would be good to ⓒextend this idea to the
amusement park design and allow visitors to create
their own paths. Upon returning to his project, he
ⓓinstructed the construction team to plant grass in
areas where he wanted to create the pathways.
When the grass started to grow, he opened the
amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some wide and
some narrow, because they were formed naturally
by visitors. The following year, Gropius used the
grass pathways as an ⓔoutline on which he built
permanent
pathways,
(E)resulted
in
the
most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
was later chosen as the best road design at the
1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium
in London.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ attraction: a place or facility in an amusementpark that people visit for enjoyment
ⓑ pick: to remove fruit from a plant by handfor use or eating
ⓒ extend: to make a business, an idea, aninfluence, etc. cover more areas oroperate in more places
ⓓ instruct: to give official directions or ordersabout what should be done
ⓔ outline: a brief summary showing the mainpoints or structure of something
solution: ⓔ outline은 ‘윤곽(선)’이라는 뜻으로 쓰였으나, ‘a brief summary showing the main points or structure of something(어떤 것 의 주요 요점이나 구조를 보여 주는 간단한 요약)’은 outline의 또 다른 뜻인 ‘개요’에 대한 영영풀이이므로 알맞지 않다. ’a line around the edge of something which shows its shape (어떤 것의 형태를 보여주는 그것의 가장자리 주변의 선)‘과 같 은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

G: Coach, can I talk to you?
M: What’s wrong? Is everything okay?
G: I just don’t think I’m good at swimming.
M: Oh, come on. What makes you think that?
G: I try my best, but I’m not getting any better.
M: Anne, (A)don’t throw in the towel yet. I know
you devote more time and effort into swimming
than anyone.
G: I do, but I’m worried that my times are not
getting any faster. What should I do?
M: Don’t despair. How about coming to the
swimming pool an hour earlier and practicing
more? I’ll help you.
G: Okay. With more practice, I’m sure my times will
improve. I will come early tomorrow.
M: That’s the attitude. I’m sure all your blood,
sweat, and tears will pay off.

While it is true that individual skills are the most
important in the world of sports, having a partner
who can cooperate with the player with those skills
is equally important. In a marathon, a key reason a
front runner can reach the finish line after that long
journey is the presence of a pacemaker. The
pacemaker helps maintain a steady pace for the
front runner, shielding the front runner from the
headwind. Without the pacemaker, the front runner
has to cope with the harsh wind alone and put in
extra effort to maintain the pace. In Formula One,
the world’s largest car race series, each team enters
two cars. Both drivers try their best for victory, but
for the team’s win, one person employs strategies
such as blocking or obstructing other vehicles so
that their teammate can get ahead. In rock
climbing, individual skills are essential, but when a
mistake is made, the person referred to as the
belay partner manages the rope to prevent a fall.
Similarly, in the case of scuba diving, all divers are
paired up with a dive companion called a “buddy.”
The buddies are responsible for each other’s safety.
No matter how exceptional your skills may be, you
cannot do it alone.
choices: the diverse history and rules of global sports
the vital role of partners and cooperation insports
comparison of safety measures in extreme sports
the difference in strategy between individual andteam sports
why individual talent is more important thancooperation in professional athletics

body:
While it is true that individual skills are the most
important in the world of sports, having a partner
who can cooperate with the player with those skills
is equally important. In a marathon, a key reason a
front runner can reach the finish line after that long
journey is the presence of a pacemaker. The
pacemaker helps maintain a steady pace for the
front runner, shielding the front runner from the
headwind. Without the pacemaker, the front runner
has to cope with the harsh wind alone and put in
extra effort to maintain the pace. In Formula One,
the world’s largest car race series, each team enters
two cars. Both drivers try their best for victory, but
for the team’s win, one person employs strategies
such as blocking or obstructing other vehicles so
that their teammate can get ahead. In rock
climbing, individual skills are essential, but when a
mistake is made, the person referred to as the
belay partner manages the rope to prevent a fall.
Similarly, in the case of scuba diving, all divers are
paired up with a dive companion called a “buddy.”
The buddies are responsible for (A)___________________
______________________. (B)당신의 기량이 아무리 뛰어나
다고 하더라도, 당신은 혼자서 그것을 할 수 없습니다.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: each other’s safety
obstructing other divers
the display of diving skills
their personal athletic goals
the speed of underwater exploration
solution: 암벽 등반에서 실수가 발생했을 때 빌레이 파트너로 불리는 사람 이 추락을 방지하기 위해 로프를 관리한다고 한 뒤 Similarly (마찬가지로)로 스쿠버 다이빙의 ‘버디’라는 다이빙 동반자에 관해 이야기했으므로, 버디는 서로의 안전을 책임진다는 흐름 이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❶ ‘서로의 안전’이 알맞다.

My name is Bliksem, which means “lightning.” My
parents named me this because they wanted me to
be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands,
a country with more bicycles than people, I learned
to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I
loved feeling the breeze in my hair.
(A) Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than
ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at
the finish line. As promised, he handed me his
autograph saying, “You outran the others by
two laps! You’re a real racer, kid!”
(B) My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world
champion, was standing there! I ran over and
asked, “You’re Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I
have your autograph?” He smiled and said, “If
you win, you can.”
(C) When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was
held in our small town. I entered the race as
the youngest rider. Before the race started, I
looked around the crowd, and I couldn’t believe
my eyes!

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

활용한다. (→ 사이클 세계 챔 피언 Gabriel Martinez) ② 'Bliksem'의 의미는 무엇인가? (→ 번개) ④ Bliksem은 주니어 자전거 경주에서 몇 위를 차지했 는가? (→ 첫 번째로 들어와서 1위를 차지하여 우승) ⑤ Bliksem이 주니어 자전거 경주에 참가했을 때 그의 나이는 몇 살이었는가? (→ 열한 살) 20) ④: 앞서 산악 경주에서 뒤처지는 화자에게 Gabriel은 언덕 을 오르는 것은 고통스럽지만, 정상에서 보는 경치는 환상적이니 페달 밟는 것을 절대 멈추지 말라고 했다고 했으며, 뒤에는 화자는 모든 훈련 과정, 특히 언덕길 훈 련에 더욱 열심히 참여해서 마침내 산악 코스 중 하나 에서 결실을 맺었다는 내용이 이어지므로, Gabriel의 격 려가 화자에게 동기부여가 되었다는 흐름이 되어야 한 다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ④ ‘Gabriel의 격려에 힘입어’가 알 맞다. 오답 ① Gabriel의 조언을 무시해서 ② 제 공연에 좌절해서 ③ Gabriel의 꾸중에 기분이 상해서 ⑤ 다른 사이클 선수들의 성과를 질투해서

body:
As we go through life, we may become stuck in a
routine, missing out on extraordinary ideas or
solutions. In such a situation, we can try considering
things from an ⓐunconventional angle. By doing
so, we can expand our understanding of the world,
challenge
our
assumptions,
and
find
creative
solutions to problems. Let’s look at two stories that
ⓑdemonstrate the power of thinking differently.
Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this expert architect was
once ⓒtroubled when designing an amusement
park. He finished most of the main structures
except for the pathways between the attractions.
Gropius wanted to find the best design for the
pathways but could not come up with anything that
satisfied him.
One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye
because (A)_____________________________________________.
It turned out that the elderly couple who owned
the vineyard were in ⓓdeclining health and could
not pick the grapes themselves. Instead, they let
people pick as many grapes as they wanted as long
as they put five francs in the box. The couple not
only prevented their grapes from becoming too ripe
by ⓔbanning grape picking, but they also provided
an enjoyable experience for their customers.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: customers were lining up to buy grapes fromthe vineyard
a box was installed so visitors could leave writtenorders for grapes
no grapes were being sold there, with only abox placed beside the road
grapes were already packed in boxes and readyfor delivery to nearby markets
there was a box containing notices that explainedhow grapes were grown in it천재(조수경) 2과

body:
Astonished by the elderly couple’s idea of allowing
customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it
would be (A)[reasonable / unnecessary] to extend
this idea to the amusement park design and allow
visitors to create their own paths. Upon returning
to his project, he instructed the construction team
to plant grass in areas where he wanted to create
the pathways. When the grass started to grow, he
opened the amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not (B)[varied / uniform], with some
wide and some narrow, because they were formed
naturally by visitors. The following year, ⓐGropius는
잔디 오솔길들을 영구적인 통행로들을 만든 윤곽선으
로 사용했고, 그 결과 가장 편리하면서 효율적인 경로
들이 되었다. This pathway design was later chosen
as the best road design at the 1971 International
Landscape Architecture Symposium in London.
It was (C)[consistent / inconsistent] with common
sense to allow people to walk on newly sprouted grass
because it could damage the grass. Moreover, it was
unprecedented for an architect to let people do the
designing. Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into
creating ideal pathways by thinking outside the box.

(A)             (B)             (C)
choices: unnecessary    uniforminconsistent
reasonable    uniforminconsistent
reasonable    variedinconsistent
unnecessary    variedconsistent
reasonable    uniformconsistent

body:
Have you ever wondered why there are mirrors in
elevators? The world’s first successful passenger
elevator was installed in a five-story building in New
York in 1857. This prominent development brought
excitement to the field of architecture by making
(A)[it / that] possible to build much taller buildings
than ever before. Nevertheless, passengers were
highly dissatisfied regardless of how practical it was.
Employees of the elevator company conducted a
customer survey in order to find out why the
passengers were so unhappy. The results of the
questionnaire showed that it was the elevator’s slow
speed that (B)[was caused / was causing] dissatisfaction.
The trip from one floor to the next took nearly
fifteen seconds. The employees also discovered that
passengers thought the elevator was much slower
than it actually was because passengers had nothing
to do. During the slow ride, some passengers
complained
and
said
they
felt
(C)[trapping
/
trapped]. Even though the employees identified
speed as the main source of dissatisfaction, it was
not something that could be improved immediately
due to technological limitations.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)               (B)               (C)
choices: itwas causing  trapped
thatwas caused  trapping
itwas causing  trapping
thatwas causing  trapped
itwas caused  trapped
solution: (A) 동명사 making의 목적어 자리이며, 뒤에 목적격보어인 형 용사 possible과 to build 이하의 to부정사구가 진목적어로 이 어지므로, ‘make+가목적어(it)+목적격보어+진목적어(to부정사)(~ 을 …하게 만들다)’ 구문을 이루는 가목적어로 it이 알맞다. (B) ‘it-that’ 강조 구문의 it was와 that 사이에 강조되는 주어 the elevator’s slow speed가 ‘초래하고 있었던’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어로 명사 dissatisfaction이 이어지므로, 과거진행형인 was causing이 알맞다. (C) said의 목적어절에 쓰인 동사 felt의 보어 역할을 하는 분 사 자리로, 목적어절의 주어 they(=some passengers)가 ‘갇히 는’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 trapped가 알맞다.

Then, one day, one employee of the elevator
company began to look at the problem from a
different perspective. She thought about it from a
passenger’s point of view. She thought that what
mattered was not speed but ⓐ_______________________.
She asked herself what could be done in this case.
After many days of searching for a solution, she
proposed installing a mirror inside the elevator. She
believed that it could make the elevator appear
larger, reducing the feeling of being trapped. Also,
she believed that people could relieve boredom by
looking in the mirror.
On a survey done after the mirror was installed,
passengers commented on how much faster the
new elevator was, even though the speed was
exactly
the
same.
Passengers
stopped
paying
attention to the speed of the elevator because they
were looking in the mirror.
ⓑ만약 그 직원이 그 문제를 해결하기 위해 그 엘리
베이터의 속도를 높이는 방법들만 생각했다면, 해결책

body:
Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this expert architect was
once troubled when ⓐdesigned an amusement
park. He finished most of the main structures
except for the pathways between the attractions.
Gropius wanted to find the best design for the
pathways but could not come up with anything that
satisfied him.
One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to ⓑwas famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye
because there was no one selling grapes but only a
box by the side of the road. It turned out that the
elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
themselves. Instead, they let people pick as ⓒmany
grapes as they wanted as long as they put five
francs in the box. The couple not only prevented
their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting
grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable
experience for their customers.
Astonished by the elderly couple’s idea of allowing
customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it
would be good to extend this idea to the
amusement park design and ⓓallow visitors to
create their own paths. Upon returning to his
project, he instructed the construction team to plant
grass in areas where he wanted to create the
pathways. When the grass started to grow, he
opened the amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some ⓔwidely
and some narrow, because they were formed
naturally by visitors. The following year, Gropius
used the grass pathways as an outline ⓕwhere he
built permanent pathways, resulting in the most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
was later chosen as the best road design at the
1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium
in London.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people
to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could
damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented
for an architect ⓖletting people do the designing.
Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating
ideal pathways by thinking outside the box.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Finding Ideal Routes by Observing Notable Architects
Overcoming a Design Challenge Through InventiveThinking
Drawbacks Resulting from a Shift in Perspectivein Pathway Design

(B) 주어부 cultures with low uncertainty avoidance의 핵심인 복수명사 cultures에 수일치한 복수동사 are와 등위 접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 동사 자리이므로, 복수 동사 show가 적절하다. (C) ‘focus on ~(~에 초점을 맞추다)’의 표현을 이루는 전치사 on의 목적어 자리에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is happening now)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함하여 ‘~한 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what이 적절하다.

body:
All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
what people value. A psychologist who (A)[named /
was named] Geert Hofstede became interested in
cataloging these invisible cultural features, and he
came up with a number of categories. According to
him, a cultural difference can be found regarding
uncertainty avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers
to how well people of a certain culture tolerate the
unexpected.
Cultures
with
high
uncertainty
avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or
unknown events. Thus, they tend to have strict
standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures with
low uncertainty avoidance are more open to the
unknown and (B)[show / shows] more acceptance to
things that are different. This is why these cultures
tend to impose fewer regulations. Another feature
that distinguishes cultures is their orientation of
temporal horizon, or how they relate to time.
Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the
present over the future. Since they are more
focused on (C)[that / what] is happening now, they
place more stress on having immediate outcomes.
However, cultures with long-term orientation value
the future over the present. In these cultures,
people are likely to delay short-term results in favor
of long-term ones.

pay (사역동사 make가 수동태로 쓰인 are made에 이어져 있으며, ‘make+목적어+목적격보어 (동사원형)(~가 …하게 하다)’의 목적격보어인 동사원형 은 수동태에서는 to부정사 형태로 ‘be made+to부정사 (…하게 되다)’와 같이 써야 하므로 paying을 to pay로 고친다.) ⓖ appreciating → appreciate 또는 to appreciate ( ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 돕다, ~가 … 하는 데 도움이 되다)’의 5형식 구문에서 준사역동사 help의 목적격보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 써야 하 므로, help와 목적어인 you 뒤의 appreciating을 동사원 형 appreciate나 to부정사인 to appreciate로 고친다.) *원래 지문에는 appreciate가 쓰였음 오답 ⓐ ’one of+복수명사(구)‘가 주어일 때 이어지는 동사의 수는 단수인 one에 일치시켜야 하므로, 과거시제 단수 동사 was로 수일치 시킨 뒤, 보어 자리에 명사적 용법 의 to부정사 to forbid를 쓴 was to forbid는 적절하다. ⓑ 이어지는 that절이 나타내는 사실에 대해 이전에 ‘들 었을지도 모른다’라고 가정하며 설명을 이어가는 흐름 이므로, 과거 사실에 대한 약한 추측을 나타내는 ‘may have p.p.(~했을지도 모른다)’를 사용한 may have heard는 적절하다. ⓔ ‘~을 고려하면’이라는 뜻으로 전치사와 같은 역할을 해 뒤의 명사구 the large number of tourists from all over the world를 목적어로 취하며, 주절인 ‘it is ~ monuments’ 앞에서 비인칭독립분사구문을 이루는 Considering은 적절하다. 참고로, 분사구문의 의미상 주 어가 주절의 주어와 상관없이 생략되고 관용적으로 쓰 이는 분사구문을 비인칭독립분사구문이라고 한다. ⓕ appear는 불완전 자동사로 쓰일 때 to부정사(구)를 보어로 취해 ‘appear+to부정사(구)(~인 것처럼 보이다, ~인 것 같다)’와 같이 쓸 수 있으며, 뒤에 형용사 difficult가 이어지므로, 형용사를 보어로 취할 수 있는 동사 be의 to부정사인 to be는 적절하다. 12) ⑤: 세계 각국의 사람들이 방문하는 이탈리아의 수도 로마 에서 일부 관광객들의 행동으로 인해 도시의 역사적인 건축물들이 심각한 피해를 입으면서 유적지를 보호하 기 위한 법들을 제정해야 했고, 이에 따라 다리에 자물 쇠를 다는 행위, Trevi 분수에 들어가는 것, Spanish 계 단에 앉는 것이 금지되었다는 내용이 앞에 언급되었으 므로, 그러한 법들이 현재 도시의 유적지를 보호하고 있다고 결론짓는 흐름이 되는 ⑤ ‘도시의 역사적인 기 념물을 보호하는 데 전념하고 있다’가 빈칸에 알맞다. 오답 ① 로마의 문화적 전통을 강조함으로써 더 많은 관광 객을 끌어들이는 것을 목표로 한다 ② 방문객들의 편의와 전반적인 경험을 개선하기 위해 만들어졌다 ③ 대중의 행동에 대한 정부의 권위를 보여 준다 ④ 로마의 현대적인 도시 환경을 보존하기 위해 설계 되었다 13) ⑤: <Amazing World>의 진행자가 스위스, 싱가포르, 이탈 리아 출신의 초대 손님들을 소개하고 그들이 오늘 전 세계의 흥미로운 법들에 대해 자국의 문화적, 역사적 배경을 바탕으로 그것들이 왜 만들어졌는지를 설명할 것이라고 소개한 뒤, 초대 손님 중 한 명인 Matilde에 게 스위스의 법을 공유해달라고 요청하고 있으므로, 바 로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 ⑤ ‘문화적 그리고 역사적 배 경에 의해 형성된 스위스의 독특한 법’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 전 세계의 규칙과 사회적 행동에 대한 다양한 관점 ② 공공의 편의와 관련된 널리 받아들여진 규제 ③ 사회적 규율과 관련된 스위스의 한 법의 약점들 ④ 현대적 사회 가치에 의해 영향을 받은 유럽의 인기 있는 규제 14) ③: ⓑ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to own과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로, to부정사에서 to가 생략된 동사원형인 raise는 알맞다. ⓓ 뒤에 단수인 부정대명사 one이 이어져 있으므로, ‘또 하나의 다른 ~’이라는 뜻으로 단수명사나 단수 대 명사를 수식하는 another는 알맞다. ⓕ ‘require+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(…가 ~하도록 요구하다)’의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 수동형 to부정사 to be microchipped와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 있으며, 목적어 all dogs가 ‘등록되는’ 대상이므로, to be의 과거분사 microchipped 와 연결되어 수동형 to부정사를 이루는 과거분사 registered는 알맞다. 오답 ⓐ earns → earning 또는 which earns (동사(is)가 있는 완전한 절(it is ~ countries)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사구가 이어질 수 없으므로, 주절 주어 it을 부 연 설명하는 분사구문이나 관계사절을 이루어야 한다. 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 it이 가리 키는 Switzerland가 ‘얻는’ 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 명 사구 the support of many animal lovers가 오므로, earns를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 earning으로 고치거 나, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which와 선행사인 it에 수일치한 단수동사 earns를 사용해 which earns로 고친다.) *원래 지문에는 earning이 쓰였음 ⓒ leaving → left (부사절 접속사 if 뒤에 주어와 동사 가 있는 완전한 절이 와야 하나, 뒤에 다른 동사 없이 부사 alone만 있으므로 주어를 이루는 동명사 leaving 이 될 수 없으며, 접속사 if 뒤에 ‘주어+be동사’를 생략 하고 ‘접속사+분사 ~’ 형태로 쓸 수 있으므로 분사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 생략된 주어가 주절에 해당하는 ‘social animals ~ loneliness’의 주어와 동일한 social animals이고, ‘남겨진’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, leaving을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 left로 고친다.) ⓔ would have fined → would have been fined (앞의 Otherwise가 흐름상 ‘그렇지 않았다면’이라는 뜻으로 ‘또 다른 한 마리를 데려오지 않았다면’이라는 의미를 나타내 가정법의 if절을 대신하며, 이에 상응하는 주절 의 내용 또한 과거 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, 가 정법 과거완료인 ‘If+S+had+p.p., 주어+조동사의 과거형 +have+p.p.(만약 ~했다면, …했을 텐데)’의 ‘조동사의 과 거형+have+p.p.’가 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, 주어 I가 ‘벌 금이 부과되는’ 대상이므로, would have fined를 수동태 (be p.p.)를 사용해 would have been fined로 고친다.) 15) ②: (A) 뒤에 In fact(실제로)를 사용해 스위스는 세계에서 가장 동물 친화적인 나라 중 하나로 많은 동물 애호가 들의 지지를 받고 있다고 부연 설명하므로, 스위스가 인간뿐만 아니라 동물의 복지에도 매우 신경을 쓰고 있다는 흐름이 되는 concerned(관심을 쏟는, 신경을 쓰 는)가 알맞다. unconcerned 무관심한 (B) 금붕어, 토끼, 기니피그 같은 사회적 동물을 반드시 쌍으로 기르도록 하는 법을 This law로 가리켜 ‘이러한 법’이 바탕을 두고 있는 생각을 설명하는 흐름이므로, 사회적 동물이 혼자일 때 외로움을 겪게 될 것이라고 인식한다는 흐름이 되는 experience(~을 경험하다)가 알맞다. overcome ~을 극복하다 (C) 개의 불법 거래를 막기 위해 모든 개에게 마이크로 칩을 삽입하여 국가 데이터베이스에 등록할 것을 요구 하는 법을 예시로 들고 있으므로, 동물의 삶의 질을 보 장하는 추가적인 법이 있다고 소개하는 흐름이 되는 guarantee(~을 보장하다)가 알맞다. undermine ~을 약화시키다 16) examples of Switzerland’s various laws valuing the well-being of animals 제시문 동물들의 복지를 중요하게 여기는 스위스의 다양한 법들의 예시들 17) ⑤: ⓔ suspended(유예되는, 일시 중단되는) → implemented (시행되는) 18) ④: 싱가포르가 독립했을 당시 국가의 총리가 국가 번영을 증진하기 위해 구상한 전략 중 하나로서 언급하고 있 으며, 이를 달성하기 위해 청결과 질서를 강조하며 껌 금지령을 제정했고, 이러한 법을 통해 싱가포르가 청결 면에서 세계를 선도하며 수백만 명의 관광객을 끌어들 이는 국가가 되었다고 했으므로, 청결하고 질서 있는 나라로서 관광의 중심지가 되려는 전략을 추구했음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 (A) ‘국가를 아시아 관광객 들의 ’오아시스‘로 변모시키는 것’이 의미하는 것으로 ④ ‘청결과 질서를 기반으로 하는 아시아의 선두적인 관광지로 성장하는 것’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 안전한 환경을 통해 관광객들의 경험을 풍부하게 하는 것 ② 싱가포르의 문화와 생활 방식을 선보임으로써 관광 객을 끌어들이는 것 ③ 수도의 이전을 통해 국가의 이미지를 탈바꿈하는 것 ⑤ 무역과 사업 기회에 집중하여 선도적인 경제 강국 이 되는 것 19) ④: (A) 주격 관계대명사 who가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이 므로 선행사에 수와 태를 일치시켜야 하며, 선행사인 A psychologist가 Geert Hofstede라고 ‘이름이 붙여진’ 대 상이고, 뒤에 ‘name+목적어+목적격보어(명사)(~를 …라 고 이름 짓다)’의 목적어 없이 목적격보어인 Geert Hofstede가 바로 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be named+명사(~가 …라고 이름 지어지다)’의 수동태 was named가 적절하다. 본문변형 named → who was named (B) 주어부 cultures with low uncertainty avoidance의 핵심인 복수명사 cultures에 수일치한 복수동사 are와 등위 접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 동 사 자리이므로, 복수동사 show가 적절하다. (C) ‘focus on ~(~에 초점을 맞추다)’의 표현을 이루는 전치사 on의 목적어 자리에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is happening now)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루어야 하 므로, 선행사를 포함하여 ‘~한 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what이 적절하다. 20) ④: 모든 문화가 서로 다른 독특한 특성을 가지고 있고, 언 어나 옷차림과 같이 어떤 특성은 눈에 보이는 반면 중 요하게 여기는 가치와 같이 숨겨진 특성도 있으며, 이 러한 보이지 않는 문화적 특성들과 관련해 심리학자 Geert Hofstede가 문화적 차이를 이해하는 기준으로 제시한 불확실성 회피와 시간 지향성의 개념에 대해 다 루고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ④ ‘문화적 차이를 이해하 기 위한 기준과 특성’이 알맞다. 오답 ① 가치와 규범은 어떻게 문화를 넘어 개인의 행동에 영향을 미치는가 ② 보이지 않는 문화적 힘에 의해 형성된 인간 행동의 차이 ③ 눈에 보이는 문화적 요소들이 사회적 정체성을 형성 하는 과정 ⑤ 서로 다른 사회는 어떻게 불확실성을 관리하고 미래 를 계획하는가

Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am
the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today.
I am honored to have been asked to give a talk.
Many of our high school student subscribers send
me messages with concerns about their future. So
today, I will talk about the value of experiences in
making a better future. For this talk, I asked my old
friends to write down stories about what they
experienced when they were younger. I would like
to start by reading them one by one.

not know what he wanted to do in the future. He

(A)[required / was required] to take could help him

fascinated with the art of producing beautiful
handwriting, also known as calligraphy, and decided
to attend a calligraphy class. He gained an
understanding of letter styles and learned to adjust
the spacing between various combinations of letters.
At that time, he did not expect that ⓐ______________
__________________________________________________________.
However,
later
when
he
developed
his
own
computer operating system, he incorporated what
he learned from that class into designing the
system. As a result, he developed his own computer
system with visually appealing letter styles. The
artistic letters became a sensation at the time and
are still widely used. His innovative incorporation of
calligraphy into the world of technology, (C)[that /
which] started from his personal interest, has inspired
many other corporations’ computer system designs.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)          (C)
choices: requiredcheckwhich
was requiredcheckthat
requiredcheckingthat
was requiredcheckingwhich
was requiredcheckwhich
solution: (A) 주어인 he가 ‘요구받는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘require +O+to부정사(~에게 …하는 것을 요구하다)’의 목적격보어에 해 당하는 to부정사 to take가 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be동사 +required+to부정사’를 이루는 was required가 알맞다. (B) start는 의미의 차이 없이 동명사와 to부정사를 모두 목적 어로 취하는 동사이므로, 앞에 주어진 to와 to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 check이 알맞다. (C) 쉼표 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(started ~ interest) 을 이끌어 앞 절의 calligraphy에 대한 부연 설명을 하는 관계 사절을 이루고 있으므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로, that은 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 사용하지 않으며, 완전한 절에 접속사 없이 쉼표로만 다른 완 전한 절이 이어질 수 없으므로 동사 started에 대한 주어인 지 시대명사 that도 될 수 없다.

Today, I attended a talk about the importance of
experiencing various things. In the talk, the guest
speaker mentioned that she decided to study math
harder to become a landscape architect. Since I
struggled with math as well, I was curious about
what efforts she made to improve. After the talk, I
asked her about them and she told me three
things she did. First, she identified the concepts she
did not fully understand. Next, she tried to
comprehend how and why such concepts were
derived. Finally, she solved numerous problem sets
related to those concepts. Her suggestions were
very helpful.

Now, let’s look at another Pointillist painting,
Women at the Well, painted in 1892 by Paul
Signac, a contemporary of Seurat.
In this work, two individuals are drawing water
from a well with a container. Behind the women
are a lighthouse and boats in the ocean. This
artwork portrays a hot sunny day in southern
France through the contrast of yellow sand and
blue ocean. Upon closer inspection, all the objects
in the picture __________________________________________.
It is worth noting that Signac did not simply paint
the grass green by combining yellow and blue.
Rather, he placed separate dots of yellow, blue, and
green next to each other. Viewers then perceive the
combination of these colors as green. Signac
changed the proportions of these colors to create
the various shades of green.

Have you ever zoomed in on a photo on your
computer screen? If not, take a look at the image
below.
When we look at the entire flower, it appears to
have a gradual change in shade. Now, zoom in on
the edge of the flower. You can see that it consists
of many square dots with distinct colors and tones.
Each tiny square dot is called a pixel.
Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors
of light: red, green, or blue. (A)________________, when
viewing digital images, we can perceive secondary
colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well.
These secondary colors are produced by putting
primary colors next to each other. When equal
amounts of red pixels and green pixels are put
together,
people
perceive
them
as
yellow.
(B)________________, people perceive the combination
of blue and green pixels as cyan, and the
combination of red and blue pixels as magenta.
Take the yellow bell pepper on the screen as an
example. We perceive the bell pepper as yellow,
but if you look at it closely, there are a lot of red
and green pixels next to each other.

painted with dots instead of dashes or lines. If you
look closer, you will notice ⓒwhat there are no

Have you ever zoomed in on a photo on your

When we look at the entire flower, it appears to
have a gradual change in shade. Now, zoom in on
the edge of the flower. You can see that it consists

Each pixel emits one of the three primary colors
of light: red, green, or blue. Nonetheless, when
viewing digital images, we can perceive secondary
colors, such as yellow, cyan, and magenta, as well.
These secondary colors are produced by putting
primary colors next to each other. When equal
amounts of red pixels and green pixels are put
together, people perceive them as yellow. Likewise,
people perceive the combination of blue and green
pixels as cyan, and the combination of red and
blue pixels as magenta. Take the yellow bell pepper
on the screen as an example. We perceive the bell
pepper as yellow, but if you look at it closely, _____
_________________________________________________________.

A pixel is a small square dot that has a distinctcolor and tone.
The three primary colors of light are made upof red, green, and blue.

People see magenta when red and blue pixelsare combined.

color theory, Seurat is known as a(n) (C)[abstract /
scientific] artist. He himself also said, “Some say

worth noting that Signac did not simply paint the
grass green by combining yellow and blue. Rather,
he placed separate dots of yellow, blue, and green
next to each other. Viewers then perceive the
combination of these colors as green. Signac
changed the proportions of these colors to create
the various shades of green.

first half of the twentieth century. However, this
new and scientific method of painting had a great
influence on later art groups. Modern artists have
adopted the basic concept of dots and applied it
to their works in a variety of shapes and forms.

am good at science, but I like drawing.

and what you like?

know what they want to become in the future.

helpful.

fascinated with the art of producing beautiful
handwriting, also known as calligraphy, and decided
to attend a calligraphy class. He gained an
understanding of letter styles and learned to adjust
the spacing between various combinations of letters.

would be useful or applicable to his life in the

own computer operating system, he incorporated
what he learned from that class into designing the
system. (B)______________, he developed his own
computer system with visually appealing letter styles.
The artistic letters became a sensation at the time
and are still widely used. His innovative incorporation
of calligraphy into the world of technology, which
started from his personal interest, has inspired many
other corporations’ computer system designs.
